papers.title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.

papers.title: Sequence-Conditioned Physics-Informed Neural Network for Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Using Charging Segments at High State of Charge
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable state of health (SOH) estimation is essential for lithium-ion battery safety and lifetime management. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) integrate battery degradation knowledge with deep learning to improve the physical consistency of SOH estimation. However, existing PINNs insufficiently capture degradation evolution across consecutive cycles and show limited applicability across battery chemistries and charge/discharge protocols. To address these issues, we propose a sequence-conditioned physics-informed neural network (SC-PINN) that uses a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to encode local degradation states and incorporates a degradation dynamics consistency constraint and a monotonic degradation prior to improve prediction accuracy and physical plausibility. We also develop a general charging feature extraction method for different battery chemistries and charge/discharge protocols, extracting unified 18-dimensional health features from charging segments at high state of charge (SOC). The method is validated using 317 batteries and 197,024 valid cycle samples covering four battery chemistries across nine representative tasks. SC-PINN achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.6285% and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.8924%, with the lowest RMSE in eight of nine tasks. Compared with other methods, the proposed method demonstrates good stability and applicability in both standard and small-sample experiments.

papers.title: Physics-informed learning of health-aware equivalent circuit parameter evolution for lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries exhibit nonlinear degradation under complex operating conditions and long-term cycling. Existing studies mainly focus on state-of-health (SOH) estimation, while continuous SOC–SOH-dependent ECM parameter representation and validation of neural-network-inverted parameters remain limited. This study proposes an ECM-PINN framework that integrates a neural network with a differentiable first-order RC model for joint SOH estimation, ECM parameter inversion, and voltage reconstruction. An SOH-guided consistency regularization is introduced to regulate excessive cross-cell parameter dispersion. The framework is evaluated on the Samsung 50E and HUST datasets. On unseen Samsung 50E cells, the Pearson correlation coefficients between the inverted and conventionally identified R 0 , R 1 , and C 1 are 0.996, 0.998, and 0.992, respectively. On the HUST dataset, the SOH estimation MAE and RMSE are 0.53% and 0.74%, while the voltage reconstruction MAE and RMSE are 20.50 mV and 26.00 mV. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can perform SOC–SOH-dependent ECM parameter inversion under both standardized HPPC and non-standard dynamic operating conditions, while maintaining stable SOH estimation and voltage reconstruction performance.

papers.title: Robust state-of-health estimation for lithium-ion batteries under stochastic loading: A physics-informed Bayesian continuous-time approach
papers.abstract: We estimate state of health (SOH), rather than safety, from five temporally causal 600-s block features: mean voltage, block Ah throughput, voltage variance, mean temperature, and cumulative Ah. The proposed Shadow-Mode CfC uses SPMe simulations only as an initialization prior and is subsequently fine-tuned on measured data. Under the fixed paper protocol with untreated reference-capacity labels and no prediction smoothing, the fixed-protocol Shadow CfC obtains RMSE 0.0320 and MAE 0.0245 on RW11. Under a separate validation-selected protocol, the validation-selected Shadow CfC obtains RMSE 0.0360 in the common baseline comparison. External leave-one-cell-out tests on CALCE and Oxford are reported as dataset-specific stress tests, not as safety certification or universal transfer. Monte Carlo dropout variability is reported descriptively because its empirical coverage is insufficient to support calibrated confidence-interval claims.

papers.title: Frequency-decoupled dynamic graph learning with degradation prior for robust state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
papers.abstract: State-of-health (SOH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries is critical for reliable battery management in energy storage systems, where SOH must be inferred from noisy multi-frequency health indicators under varying operating conditions. Existing methods often fail to decouple multi-frequency degradation information, capture dynamic couplings among health indicators, and preserve consistency with degradation mechanisms, which limits their robustness across temperatures and chemistries. To address these issues, this study proposes a degradation-prior-enhanced frequency-decoupled dynamic graph learning framework for robust SOH estimation. STL decomposition is first employed to separate low-frequency degradation trends from high-frequency fluctuations, each handled by a dedicated temporal branch. A degradation-guided dynamic graph module is then developed, integrating health-indicator coupling priors and degradation-direction consistency priors to suppress spurious correlations. Finally, degradation-guided loss terms are embedded to encourage SOH trajectories consistent with battery aging behavior. Experiments on three public datasets (NASA, CALCE, and Zhu et al. dataset) show that the proposed method achieves an average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.798%, outperforming mainstream baselines. In the cross-temperature transfer experiments, compared with the best-performing baseline GRU, the proposed method reduces the average root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) by 57.41% and 60.03%, respectively, indicating greater robustness and more reliable support for battery health management in practical battery monitoring.

papers.title: Assessing Modeling Fidelity for Long-Term Battery Energy Storage Planning: Operation, Degradation, and Temporal Representation
papers.abstract: Long-term battery energy storage system (BESS) planning often relies on simplified degradation, operational, and temporal representations to maintain computational tractability, yet their effects on lifecycle conclusions are not well understood. This paper assesses the modeling fidelity needed for long-term lifecycle evaluation of BESS designs used in planning studies. A 20-year grid-connected microgrid is sized using a degradation-naive planning model, after which the installed portfolio is fixed and evaluated through sequential lifecycle validation. The reference representation combines nonlinear calendar and cycle aging, C-rate-dependent efficiencies, state-of-health-dependent performance, self-discharge, battery replacement, and full 8,760-h chronology. Battery-model hierarchies, targeted ablations, linear degradation surrogates, health-update intervals, temporal reductions, and combined simplifications are compared using lifecycle cost, replacement timing, state of health, and energy adequacy. The reference case produces replacements in years 9 and 18, a $111.25 million lifecycle net present cost, and 24.01 MWh of cumulative energy not served. Omitting calendar aging eliminates both replacements and understates lifecycle cost by 35.1%, whereas a separately calibrated linear surrogate model reproduces both replacement years and limits the cost deviation to 0.2%, although energy not served remains 31.8% below the reference. A peak-informed calibrated 12-day representation preserves replacement timing but reports zero energy not served, while replacing the preserved peak day with the maximum daily-energy-deficit day substantially overstates energy not served because representative-day closure alters the battery state surrounding the critical event. The results show that modeling fidelity is metric-dependent and should be selected according to the lifecycle outcome to be preserved.

papers.title: In-situ polymerized fluorinated polyurethane-based gel polymer electrolyte for high-stability lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: A fluorinated polyurethane-based gel polymer electrolyte (GPE) with flame-retardant properties and high interfacial stability for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is developed by in-situ polymerization of polycaprolactriol, dicyclohexylmethane diisocyanate, and a fluorinated chain extender (octafluoro-1,6-hexanediol) in carbonate-based electrolyte. This GPE exhibits ionic conductivity of 2.78 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , oxidative stability up to 4.75 V, and a lithium ion transference number of 0.54. The introduction of fluorinated segments promotes the formation of a LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the lithium anode, effectively suppressing lithium dendrite growth. The gel polymer electrolyte enables stable cycling of Li/Li symmetric cell for over 500 h at 1 mA cm −2 . Moreover, the Li/LiFePO 4 cell achieves a capacity retention of 87.85% after 600 cycles at 2C, and Li/NCM811 cell maintains 76% capacity retention after 150 cycles at 0.5C. Furthermore, this GPE also exhibits good flame retardancy, indicating that this fluorinated polyurethane-based GPEs offer promising prospects for the application of LMBs with enhanced safety.

papers.title: Lithium-metal anode interfaces in Li-S batteries: From failure mechanisms to practical stabilization
papers.abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries are among the most promising post-lithium-ion energy storage technologies because of their extremely high theoretical specific capacity (1675 mAh g −1 ) and gravimetric energy density of 2567 Wh kg −1 . However, the use of lithium metal anodes in a high-concentration polysulfide environment is a primary limitation to the practical deployment of Li-S batteries. This is exacerbated by commercially relevant conditions of lean electrolyte operation, high sulfur loading (6-10 mg cm −2 ), and limited lithium supply. In this review, we present a holistic picture of the underlying failure processes in lithium metal degradation in the Li-S battery, focusing on lithium plating/stripping processes, SEI formation mechanisms, ion-transport heterogeneity, and chemo-mechanical instabilities. The latest developments on lithium-anode stabilization by three-dimensional current collectors and host architecture, artificial interphases, lithiophilic surface engineering, solid-state and gel-polymer electrolyte are critically evaluated. Importantly, this review emphasises the interplay between interface chemistry, transport kinetics, and structural evolution and their effect on long-term anode stability and cell performance. This review links fundamental mechanistic insights with practical engineering solutions and highlights major challenges and new opportunities for stable lithium-metal anodes under operating conditions. The perspectives discussed herein set the groundwork for designing commercially viable, high-energy-density Li-S batteries.

papers.title: Advancing Sulfide Electrolyte/Silicon-Based Anode Systems in All-Solid-State Batteries: Interface Stability, Design, and Perspectives
Rapid dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reconstruction of lithium-ion batteries using generative adversarial network
papers.abstract: As the global transition toward renewable energy accelerates, lithium-ion batteries have become indispensable for electric vehicles and grid-scale energy storage, driving urgent demand for reliable real-time battery diagnostics. Dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) can acquire impedance during operation without interrupting the load, but full-spectrum measurement is still time-consuming, especially at low frequencies. Sparse frequency sampling can shorten acquisition time, yet it often compromises the spectral completeness needed for equivalent circuit model (ECM) fitting and distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis. To address this challenge, this study develops a conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) for fast and robust reconstruction of full-spectrum DEIS from sparse frequency measurements. The DRT analysis is first used to resolve the impedance response and identify electrochemically informative relaxation features in the mid-to-high frequency region. Based on these characteristic peaks, four representative frequency points are selected as compact model inputs, thereby substantially reducing the required measurement burden while retaining critical diagnostic information. The conditional WGAN-GP then learns the nonlinear mapping between the sparse-frequency inputs and the complete DEIS. On the cell 4 test set, the proposed framework achieves R 2 values of 0.999583 for real impedance component and 0.992254 for imaginary impedance component. ECM analysis further shows that several impedance-related descriptors remain comparatively well constrained, while weakly identifiable parameters are explicitly distinguished. The framework therefore provides an experimentally supported basis for rapid, condition-aware DEIS reconstruction under dynamic operating conditions.

papers.title: Cross-Dataset Assessment of Cathode Thermal Descriptors for Whole-Cell Self-Heating Kinetics in Lithium-Ion Batteries: Onset, Reaction Magnitude, and Limits of Transferability
papers.abstract: Component calorimetry is widely used to assess the thermal stability of lithium-ion battery cathode materials, yet it remains unclear which material-scale descriptors retain consistent relationships with whole-cell self-heating kinetics across independent datasets and test protocols. Here, raw accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) and thermogravimetric/differential scanning calorimetry (TGA/DSC) data for lithium cobalt oxide (LCO), lithium iron phosphate (LFP), and nickel–cobalt–aluminum oxide (NCA) cells were reanalyzed using a physics-guided event framework. Cathode decomposition onset, event-specific apparent exothermic energy, and associated mass loss were compared with the maximum whole-cell self-heating rate. In the Sandia dataset, cathode onset and event-specific exothermic energy showed large matched-state-of-charge correlations with whole-cell self-heating kinetics (r = −0.983 and 0.980, respectively). In an independently generated dataset, the cathode–electrolyte onset relationship was substantially weaker (r = −0.376), whereas cathode–electrolyte reaction enthalpy retained a large association (r = 0.886). Rank-based sensitivity analysis preserved this contrast, whereas leave-one-chemistry-out stress tests were unstable for all three Sandia linear models, indicating that the strong within-dataset associations did not extrapolate reliably to an unseen chemistry. Because the two heat-release metrics were obtained under different sample configurations and calorimetric protocols, the cross-study comparison is interpreted at the descriptor-class level rather than as direct metric equivalence. Across the two conventional lithium-ion datasets examined, cathode-associated exothermic magnitude showed greater cross-dataset consistency than onset temperature alone. However, neither descriptor supported a universal chemistry-independent scaling law, indicating that component-to-cell relationships remain dependent on experimental protocol, electrode interactions, cell architecture, and battery platform.

papers.title: Space Charge Layer and Facile Halide Rearrangement Enable Fast Lithium-Ion Transport at Halide Solid Electrolyte Interfaces
papers.abstract: Halide solid electrolytes are promising candidates for energy-dense all-solid-state batteries because they combine high-voltage stability, facile processing, and fast Li-ion conduction. A recent study showed that physically mixing two halide solid electrolytes, Li$_2$ZrCl$_6$ (LZC) and Li$_3$YCl$_6$ (LYC), raises the Li-ion conductivity by 46% and 58% relative to LZC and LYC, respectively, suggesting that halide heterointerfaces offer a new route to faster ion transport; however, the origin of this enhancement remains unknown. Here, we combine density functional theory calculations, defect thermodynamics, machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics, and vibrational and Raman spectroscopy to elucidate Li-ion transport in LZC, LYC, and their heterointerface. Using low-energy ordered supercells that represent the configurational disorder of these halides, we find that Li and Cl interstitials are the dominant charged defects in both materials. Forming an LZC|LYC interface favors the generation of interfacial Li Frenkel pairs, producing Li interstitials in LZC and Li vacancies in LYC, thereby increasing the charge-carrier concentration near the interface. By analyzing the angular orientations of Cl around the metal cations in molecular dynamics trajectories of a coherent interface, we show that the interface creates new stable Cl configurations that accommodate the framework rearrangement accompanying Li hops. Simulated vibrational power spectra and measured Raman spectra indicate lattice softening and octahedral distortion at the interface, consistent with the formation of these Cl configurations. These results support a cooperative mechanism in which space charge layer formation and a dynamically flexible interfacial halide framework enhance Li-ion conduction, providing atomistic design principles for superionic halide heterostructures and multicomponent solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Piecewise Arrhenius–Long Short-Term Memory Residual Correction Modeling for Whole-Life State of Health Estimation and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries exhibit nonlinear capacity degradation under variable-temperature and complex operating conditions, which makes remaining useful life (RUL) prediction challenging. To address this issue, we propose a hybrid Arrhenius-long short-term memory (LSTM) method that combines piecewise Arrhenius thermal-damage modeling with LSTM-based residual correction. The method constructs a piecewise Arrhenius capacity-degradation model around the knee point and introduces an equivalent thermal-damage factor to accumulate temperature-induced aging effects. An LSTM residual branch then learns the discrepancy between measured capacity and the physical baseline from historical capacity, temperature, voltage, current, and prior physical predictions. A three-stage optimization strategy, comprising physical-parameter pre-fitting, residual-branch training, and physics-constrained joint fine-tuning, stabilizes residual learning while preserving mechanistic interpretability. Experiments on four CALCE CX2 validation cells yield mean SOH RMSE and MAE values of 0.020 and 0.016, respectively. The corresponding mean RUL RMSE and MAE are 41.52 and 31.58 cycles. Compared with Ade-lwT, the proposed method reduces mean SOH RMSE and MAE by 22.33% and 35.05%, respectively. For RUL prediction, the corresponding reductions are 58.06% and 62.29%. These results support the effectiveness of coupling a piecewise Arrhenius baseline with capacity-residual learning for cross-cell SOH estimation and RUL prediction.

papers.title: Aging modeling of lithium-ion cells by integrating active material loss, electrolyte degradation, solid electrolyte interphase growth, and lithium plating
papers.abstract: Multiple interrelated degradation mechanisms, heavily dependent on temperature, current rate, and rest periods, govern the performance and lifetime of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). This study extends a previously established modeling framework, initially focused on loss of Lithium inventory (LLI) from solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth and Lithium plating, to include a more comprehensive suite of degradation pathways. Specifically, the solvent-diffusion-limited SEI growth (SD) and combined calendar and cyclic aging (CCC) models are enhanced to incorporate loss of active material (LAM) driven by diffusion-induced mechanical stress. Additionally, the framework now accounts for electrolyte depletion and the loss of electrical connectivity. Electrolyte consumption from SEI thickening and Lithium plating is dynamically modeled via a depletion factor, capturing the cascading effects on transport properties and accelerated aging. The proposed models are validated against experimental data from 43 Ah automotive-grade Li-ion pouch cells. These cells were cycled at 10 °C using optimized charging profiles ranging from 50% to 150% of the experimentally determined Lithium plating current limit. To assess predictive accuracy, results are benchmarked against both experimental trends and the original SD and CCC modeling frameworks. Simulations demonstrate how degradation pathways shift under varying charging intensities. While lower current rates mitigate Lithium plating risks, degradation continues through SEI thickening and progressive LAM. Conversely, at higher current rates, Lithium plating accelerates electrolyte depletion. This triggers a self-reinforcing feedback loop that amplifies LAM. Temperature variations further modulate these trends by modifying intercalation kinetics and mechanical stress evolution. Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) analysis of the capacity fade (SoH C ) confirms that the enhanced models achieve errors within 5% across all charging strategies. This accuracy demonstrates the framework’s robustness in capturing long-term degradation dynamics. By highlighting the critical interplay between Lithium plating, SEI growth, LAM, and electrolyte depletion, this study provides a mechanistic foundation for developing optimized battery management and fast-charging strategies.

papers.title: An empirical model for deriving information on ion dynamics from $μ$SR data via the conventional Kubo-Toyabe function analysis
papers.abstract: We present an empirical model that analytically relates the parameters of the extended Kubo-Toyabe (KT) function $G_z^{\rm EA}(t;Δ,ν_{\rm i},Q)$, which describes muon spin relaxation ($μ$SR) induced by jump diffusion of ions using the Edwards-Anderson parameter $Q$, to those of the conventional KT function $G_z^{\rm KT}(t;Δ_{\rm KT},ν_{\rm KT})$ that serves as an approximation of $G_z^{\rm EA}(t)$. The proposed formulae successfully reproduce the anomalous temperature dependences of the linewidth $Δ_{\rm KT}(T)$ and the fluctuation rate $ν_{\rm KT}(T)$ which are artifacts observed upon analyzing $μ$SR data on ion diffusion using $G_z^{\rm KT}(t)$. Applying this model to $Δ_{\rm KT}$ and $ν_{\rm KT}$ published in the literature of battery materials yields activation energy $E_{\rm i}$ and pre-exponential factor $ν_{\rm i0}$ in the Arrhenius equation for ion diffusion, $ν_{\rm i}(T)=ν_{\rm i0} e^{-E_{\rm i}/kT}$, that are in excellent agreement with those deduced using other techniques, transforming peculiar artifacts into a powerful diagnostic tool.

papers.title: Fast charging of quantum batteries assisted by nonlinear couplings
papers.abstract: Charger-mediated quantum batteries offer promising opportunities for efficient energy transfer and storage at the quantum level, with potential advantages beyond their classical counterparts. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that nonlinear charger-battery interactions can substantially accelerate the charging of quantum batteries. In the weak-driving regime, sufficiently strong nonlinear coupling can dominate over the effect of dephasing and significantly reduce the charging time. In the strong- and optimal-driving regimes, where the optimal driving strength maximizes the steady-state ergotropy in the linear-coupling regime, nonlinear coupling gives rise to a new optimum in the charging time beyond that of the linear-coupling regime, accompanied by nearly critically damped dynamics. Remarkably, even in the absence of external driving, nonlinear coupling alone can substantially reduce the charging time, providing an alternative route toward fast battery charging. Our results establish nonlinear charger-battery coupling as an effective resource for accelerating quantum-battery charging and broaden the scope of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer and storage.

papers.title: A Fusion State-of-Charge Estimation Framework for Lithium-Ion Batteries of Electric Vehicles Using Enhanced Single Particle Model and CNN-BiLSTM
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is critical for driving range prediction and battery safety in lithium-ion electric vehicles. Purely data-driven methods often lack physical interpretability, whereas electrochemical models are limited by model complexity, parameter identification, and real-time computational burden. This study proposes a physics-guided SOC estimation framework that integrates an enhanced single-particle model (ESPM) with a convolutional bidirectional long short-term memory network (CNN-BiLSTM). The ESPM incorporates electrolyte-phase dynamics and derives electrode utilization variables to describe internal electrochemical states. These physically meaningful variables are combined with measured current, voltage, and temperature as hybrid inputs, while Bayesian optimization is used to tune key hyperparameters. Experiments are performed on A123 lithium iron phosphate cells under FUDS, DST, and US06 profiles from −10 to 40 °C. The proposed framework limits maximum relative SOC errors to 4% under DST and 3% under US06, with maximum RMSE and MAE values of 1.35% and 1.08%. Compared with LSTM, GRU, and CNN-BiLSTM baselines, the framework improves estimation accuracy by 15.16% to 51.06%, demonstrating improved robustness under dynamic and wide-temperature conditions.

papers.title: Mechanism-Guided Alkaline Leaching of Al–Si Alloy Enables High-Purity Porous Silicon Anodes for Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Selective alkaline leaching of Al–Si alloys is a simple and economical route for producing porous silicon. However, the mechanism governing aluminium hydroxide (gibbsite) formation and its suppression during leaching remains poorly understood. This work develops a mechanism-guided alkaline leaching strategy for producing high-purity porous silicon from an Al–Si alloy. The effects of KOH concentration, solution volume, and leaching conditions on aluminium dissolution and gibbsite formation were systematically investigated. Regulated-pH experiments, phase analysis, and shrinking-core kinetic modelling revealed that gibbsite precipitation originates from localized pH gradients near the solid–liquid interface. Vigorous agitation and optimised alkaline conditions suppress gibbsite formation by enhancing mass transport. The optimised porous silicon was subsequently purified by acid leaching and systematically characterised to confirm its high purity and porous architecture. As a lithium-ion battery anode, the porous silicon delivered an initial discharge capacity of approximately 2752 mAh g-1, an initial coulombic efficiency of 80.56%, stable cycling over 300 cycles, and a high-rate capacity of approximately 580 mAh g -1 at 5 A g -1 . The mechanistic understanding provides practical guidelines for scalable, HF-free production of high-purity porous silicon and demonstrates its potential for high-capacity lithium-ion battery applications.

papers.title: NOCE-Net: Representation Learning for Battery Operational Context via Nested Sequence Modelling
papers.abstract: Learning effective representations from battery operational history is essential for predictive health management and control-oriented applications. Existing approaches rely on response-dependent engineered features or short early-life windows, limiting generalisability and precluding use in prospective settings where future responses are unavailable. We propose NOCE-Net, a deep nested sequence model that learns control-enabling representations directly from raw cyclic operational or telemetric data. Our data pipeline, re-BatteryData, standardises heterogeneous aging datasets into semantically equivalent Full Equivalent Cycles (FECs) defined by absolute charge throughput, enabling end-to-end learning across diverse operational regimes. NOCE-Net combines multi-patch transformer encoders for intra-cycle dynamics with a GRU backbone for inter-cycle state evolution, operating on approximately $700$ batteries across ten public datasets spanning over $300$ operational profiles. In zero-shot evaluation on unseen battery chemistries and usage patterns, NOCE-Net achieves $13.7\%$ MAPE in voltage response prediction, outperforming strong long-sequence baselines by over $43\%$ while using $40 \times$ fewer parameters. Shape and component diagnostics of the learned hidden states reveal that the GRU's principal direction of evolution achieves Spearman $|ρ| \geq 0.95$ with the capacity fade trajectory on average across all datasets with monotone degradation profiles, including zero-shot test batteries, providing evidence that the representations encode degradation dynamics transferable to downstream tasks beyond battery response modelling. Code is available at https://github.com/BeArnab96/NOCE-Net.

papers.title: A practical route to amorphous solid-state electrolyte structures by hybrid reverse Monte Carlo with foundation potentials
papers.abstract: Amorphous alkali oxychlorides are fast ion conductors, but their atomic structure remains unresolved. Total scattering sums all partial pair correlations into one curve that has no unique inversion, so the structure must be modeled. Melt-quench molecular dynamics builds a model from the interatomic potential alone, and reverse Monte Carlo (RMC) builds one from the measurement alone. The two have rarely been compared with all else held fixed. We benchmark both routes and two hybrid schemes on amorphous \ce{Li_{0.9}NbO_{0.9}Cl_{4.1}} against one neutron pair distribution function with one foundation potential. The hybrid schemes put the energy either in the acceptance rule (inline) or in short relaxations between blocks of refinement (alternating). Each refinement starts from a melt-quench glass or from a random packing of isolated units. The glass has the lowest energy and places the first-shell peaks correctly, but carries almost none of the oscillation beyond 6~Å (goodness of fit $R^{2} = 0.29$). Pure RMC fits the measurement to within its counting noise ($R^{2} = 0.99$), but at more than $1.3$~eV/atom above the glass, and niobium loses about half of its first-shell chlorine. Started from the glass, both hybrid schemes reach $R^{2} = 0.92$ within $0.1$~eV/atom of its energy and keep its coordination chemistry. Structures from the two inputs fit almost equally well and differ in energy by a tenth of the RMC penalty, yet they differ in whether their polyhedra are connected. The input is therefore part of the method. We recommend quenching a glass with a foundation potential and refining it against the measurement with a hybrid scheme. The resulting structure carries both the local chemistry and the medium-range order, and it is the starting point for modeling ion transport in these conductors.

papers.title: ECMpare: A systematic framework for comparing parameter estimation methods in lithium-ion battery equivalent circuit models
papers.abstract: Accurate parameter estimation of equivalent circuit models (ECMs) is essential for reliable electrochemical modelling, control, and state of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries. This work presents a systematic comparison framework for least-squares-based parameter estimation methods applied to Thevenin-type ECMs (0RC, 1RC, and 2RC). A physics-informed synthetic dataset is generated using a many-particle Doyle-Fuller-Newman (MP-DFN) model implemented in PyBaMM, ensuring internal electrochemical consistency while enabling controlled variation of operating conditions. The framework integrates multiple estimation strategies, including linear least squares, nonlinear least squares, trust-region optimisation, and sequential least-squares programming, with consistent parameter bounds and initialisation. A cycle-based data segmentation approach is introduced to associate locally estimated parameters with specific operating conditions defined by SOC current, and temperature. SOC is derived from electrode stoichiometry, and the open-circuit voltage (OCV) is reconstructed accordingly, thereby avoiding inconsistencies associated with nominal-capacity-based definitions. The comparative analysis is performed using data generated specifically for this study from a range of dynamic protocols, including HPPC-derived, drive-cycle-based, and application-relevant load profiles, with performance evaluated using voltage-prediction error metrics. The proposed framework enables transparent and reproducible assessment of the influence of estimation method, excitation profile, and model structure on model parametrisation and predictive accuracy. Results demonstrate that both the choice of estimation algorithm and the characteristics of the input data strongly affect the convergence consistency and physical interpretability of the identified parameters. The methodology provides a generalised platform for benchmarking ECM parameter estimation techniques and supports the development of more reliable reduced-order models for electrochemical energy storage systems.

papers.title: Silicon-based anodes for lithium and sodium-ion batteries: nanoparticle design, composite engineering, failure mechanisms, and practical challenges
papers.abstract: The development of high-performance anode materials is crucial for improving the energy density and cycle life of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Silicon (Si) is a promising anode candidate because of its high theoretical capacity (~3579 mAh/g), far exceeding that of conventional carbonaceous anodes. However, its practical application is hindered by severe volume expansion during cycling, which triggers mechanical fracture, unstable interphase formation, loss of electrical contact, and rapid capacity fading. This review provides an integrated assessment of Si-based anodes for both LIBs and SIBs by linking synthesis and structural design with ion-storage mechanisms, failure behaviour, and mitigation strategies. Particular emphasis is placed on the synergies and trade-offs among carbon modification, polymer encapsulation, nanostructured/porous Si architectures, and electrolyte/interfacial engineering in simultaneously addressing mechanical, electrical, and interfacial degradation. The distinct challenges associated with Li and Na storage are critically compared, highlighting the substantially less developed understanding of Si-based anodes for SIBs. Rather than evaluating individual modification strategies in isolation, this review establishes relationships among material architecture, conductive networks, mechanical stability, and interphase chemistry and discusses their implications for practical electrode design. Finally, remaining challenges and research priorities are identified toward scalable, high-loading, interfacial stable, and sustainable Si-based anodes for next-generation energy-storage systems.

papers.title: Operando optical monitoring of chemo-mechanical degradation in silicon-carbon anode batteries for state-of-health estimation
papers.abstract: Silicon/carbon (Si/C) anodes are promising candidates for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, severe volume changes lead to chemo-mechanical degradation, which is difficult to observe using conventional external monitoring approaches and hinders accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation consequently. In this study, embedded Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors are employed for operando monitoring of the internal strain evolution of Si/C-anode pouch cells, enabling the investigation of chemo-mechanical degradation mechanisms and the development of a strain-informed SOH estimation framework. Crucially, Si/C-anode cells exhibit higher peak and irreversible strains compared with graphite-anode cells, indicating more severe mechanical deformation during cycling. Furthermore, aging experiments reveal that the accumulated irreversible strain serves as an effective indicator of interfacial degradation. Correlation analysis demonstrates that both reversible and irreversible strains exhibit strong linear relationships with capacity degradation, with Pearson coefficients of 0.991 and −0.973, respectively. Finally, mechanically interpretable strain features are incorporated into a Ridge-regression model for SOH estimation, achieving a root mean square error of 1.255%. This study establishes an internal strain-driven diagnostic framework for revealing chemo-mechanical degradation mechanisms and enabling accurate SOH estimation of high-energy-density LIBs.

papers.title: Rational Integration of Multiple Additives for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.

papers.title: System Identification for Nonlinear Stochastic State-Space Models Using Ensemble Kalman Inversion with Application to Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Nonlinear state-space system identification has attracted decades of interest, yet remains challenging because of the interplay among unknown parameters, nonlinear dynamics, and latent state variables. Its difficulty increases dramatically when the state and parameter dimensions increase. To address this challenge, we develop an ensemble Kalman inversion (EnKI)-based approach. This approach leverages EnKI to perform maximum a posteriori parameter estimation through successive local Gaussian approximations, enabling an iterative and incremental search for unknown parameters. The search combines Monte Carlo sampling with Kalman-type updates to evolve an ensemble of parameter samples, thereby offering empirical stability and the ability to handle strongly nonlinear models. The EnKI search is coupled with state estimation conditioned on the latest parameter estimates. This enables parameter identification along with latent state recovery. To improve scalability for large datasets, we further develop a cascaded EnKI (CasEnKI) method, which assimilates subdatasets sequentially to accelerate computation. We validate the proposed methods using a lithium-ion battery model with ten state variables and 18 unknown parameters. Simulation results show that the EnKI approach offers high identification accuracy and empirical stability in parameter search. Further, experimental results illustrate the computational efficiency and scalability of the CasEnKI method for large battery datasets.

papers.title: Stable charged energy and phase transitions in an anisotropic Dicke quantum battery with Kerr nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Phase transitions (PTs) in quantum many-body systems offer a powerful route to manipulate the performance of quantum batteries (QBs). Here, we investigate an anisotropic Dicke QB with Kerr nonlinearity, focusing on the role of PTs in the charging process of the QB system. By analyzing how the Kerr nonlinearity reshapes the cavity level-spacing structure, we find that multiple near-degeneracies emerge at specific nonlinearity strengths. Away from the region of multiple near-degeneracies, the stable stored energy is governed primarily by the ergodic-nonergodic transition (ENET), whereas within this region it is controlled by first- and second-order dissipative phase transitions (DPTs). We employ Liouvillian spectral theory to quantify the critical slowing down associated with the DPTs, and use the Wigner function to characterize the properties of the cavity field in the vicinity of criticality. We optimize the charging process via reinforcement learning (RL) and reveal the physical mechanism underlying performance enhancement from the perspective of ergodic and nonergodic phase dynamics. Our results offer a feasible pathway for manipulating and optimizing quantum battery performance based on intrinsic PT behaviors.

papers.title: Degradation-informed state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries using a Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries degrade during service through coupled electrochemical and thermal aging, causing capacity fade and increased operational risk. Accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation is therefore required for battery health management. When only compact cycle-level descriptors are available, maintaining prediction accuracy together with model interpretability remains difficult. This study proposes a degradation-informed hyperparameter-optimized Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (HPO-TabPFN) framework for SOH estimation. Each cycle is represented using temporal, energy-related and incremental-capacity descriptors, chronological context is constructed for TabPFN, and inference-related hyperparameters are optimized. Grid search, random search, particle swarm optimization and Bayesian optimization (BO) are evaluated under the same temporal validation protocol. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) is used to analyze local feature attribution, and Sobol analysis is used to quantify model-output sensitivity and interaction effects. On the evaluated NASA and CALCE cell sequences, hyperparameter optimization reduced the prediction error of TabPFN, and the Bayesian-optimized model achieved average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values of 0.2450% and 0.1800%, respectively. Under the same chronological delayed-label protocol, BO-TabPFN gave the lowest error among the unoptimized TabPFN and the evaluated baseline regressors on the tested cells. These results indicate that cycling-derived health indicators can support accurate tabular SOH estimation in the evaluated public datasets, while the NASA B05 case study illustrates how the fitted estimator depends on the selected health factors under the stated attribution and sensitivity settings.

papers.title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS − readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li + , constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H 2 O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO 2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm −2 )/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF 6 ‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

papers.title: Consistent Modeling of SEI Growth via Electron Diffusion Validated Across Diverse Cell Specifications and Operating Conditions in LFP/Graphite Cells
papers.abstract: Understanding and predicting degradation in lithium-ion batteries is critical for their widespread deployment. The continuous growth of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) remains a dominant aging pathway, yet accurately modeling its kinetics across diverse cell specifications and operating conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we present and validate a physically grounded SEI growth model mediated by the electron diffusion mechanism. This framework intrinsically captures the state of charge (SOC) dependence of degradation through the impact of the anode potential on the electron concentration, which governs the rate of SEI growth. The presented model explicitly accounts for variations in electrolyte salt, anode material, temperature, and cycling rate. Validation against experimental aging data for LFP/graphite cells demonstrates high predictive accuracy across a broad range of cell specifications and cycling conditions, including confined SOC windows, electrolyte salts (LiFSI, LiPF6), artificial graphites (AGC, AGD), temperatures (40-70°C), and C-rates (C/20-1C). Remarkably, a single, consistent set of parameters is applied to simulate the capacity fade for all experiments without recalibration. While quantitative overestimations occur during high-SOC storage periods, the framework consistently captures the observed degradation trends. Our findings underscore that lower SOC operation mitigates degradation, establishing a physics-based model for predicting long-term lithium-ion battery aging.

papers.title: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
papers.abstract: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase \(γ_n\). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is \(γ_n\)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.

papers.title: Real-time state-of-health estimation and online degradation prognosis from partial battery discharge using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy sources, energy storage systems have become essential, making the accurate estimation of their State of Health (SOH) and degradation behavior critical. In this work, we propose a physics-informed deep learning approach for lithium-ion battery SOH prediction using incomplete discharge curves extracted from arbitrary voltage ranges, thereby reflecting realistic and heterogeneous operating conditions. The proposed method combines data-driven learning with physically motivated degradation dynamics to ensure consistent and reliable SOH estimation from partial discharge information, achieving a MAPE below 4$\%$. In addition, a real-time degradation trend estimation strategy is introduced to detect key aging transitions without requiring prior knowledge or historical data, making it applicable to a wide range of batteries. Overall, our approach enables SOH estimation from arbitrary discharge segments and a real-time degradation forecast that continuously integrates all usage, overcoming previous methods that rely on fixed protocols or early, non-adaptive predictions.

papers.title: Coupled Design of Silicon Anodes and Solid-State Electrolytes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Silicon-based solid-state batteries (Si-SSBs) offer enhanced safety and higher energy density over conventional liquid-electrolyte systems, yet their practical realization is critically hindered by severe volume expansion of silicon anodes and poor interfacial compatibility with solid-state electrolytes. This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of recent advances from a coupled design perspective, integrating silicon anode engineering, electrolyte compatibility optimization, and interfacial stabilization. We systematically examine emerging strategies for silicon anodes alongside compatibility approaches tailored to each electrolyte type, with a particular focus on the coupled chemo-mechanical degradation at the silicon/electrolyte interface. A systematic compatibility mapping linking different Si architectures with specific electrolyte families reveals the most promising material combinations and their underlying design principles. Beyond materials design, we address critical manufacturing challenges including stack pressure management, scalable processing, and prelithiation techniques essential for industrial translation. Finally, we propose a forward-looking roadmap integrating multiscale characterization, AI-assisted design, and scalable fabrication, providing both theoretical guidance and practical strategies for developing high-performance, commercially viable Si-SSBs.

papers.title: Feeder-Aware Service-Conditioned Flexibility of Grid-Interactive Buildings
papers.abstract: Grid-interactive buildings can adjust demand, but building-feasible power budgets may differ from accepted feeder-head offers. This study addresses a practical question: to what extent can the adjustable electricity consumption of buildings be translated into deliverable flexibility services while satisfying feeder-head operating requirements? To enable a fair comparison, we adopt the same baseline operating schedule, equipment conditions, and post-service recovery requirements for indoor temperature and battery state of charge (SOC). Flexibility is then evaluated under two settings: one considering only building-level constraints, and the other additionally accounting for feeder-head constraints. We first use a simplified network model with explicit security margins to determine a preliminary amount of flexibility that can be committed. The resulting schedule is then validated using a more detailed network simulation via Modelica. If network losses cause the actual response to deviate from the committed response, the electricity consumption of individual buildings is rescheduled. If the required response still cannot be achieved, the committed flexibility level is reduced. The experiments cover multiple service activation times, regulation directions, and service durations. For comparative purposes, we retain the initial optimization result as the reference estimate of the maximum potentially available flexibility, rather than interpreting the failure of a particular subsequent realization attempt as evidence that a larger flexibility level is inherently infeasible. The results demonstrated that 24.51\% of nonzero flexibility contracts were rejected due to feeder-head constraints, 67.04\% of contracts were accepted with some rescheduling and building redispatch, and only 8.09\% of contracts were accepted without any changes.

papers.title: Filter-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Battery Fast Charging with State of Health and Plating-Aware Reward Design
papers.abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is crucial for electric vehicle adoption, yet it increases safety risks and accelerates battery ageing. To address this, we propose a filter-augmented reinforcement learning (RL) framework for lifelong health-aware fast charging, based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm. The RL agent is guided by a reward function that balances charging speed and battery longevity through the incorporation of state of health (SoH) information and an SoH-dependent voltage penalty term derived from a constant--current constant--overpotential charging strategy. Since onboard SoH estimates are inevitably corrupted by noise, two filtering strategies are integrated: an exponential moving average (EMA) filter when noise statistics are unknown, and a Kalman filter when they are available, with the filtered estimate embedded in both the agent's state and reward computation. The RL policy is trained using data from high-fidelity life-cycle simulations. The evaluation uses a published electrochemical and degradation parameterisation for a commercial LG M50 cell. Results show that the proposed method achieves up to 21.4\% more equivalent full cycles (EFCs) than conventional constant current--constant voltage (CC--CV) charging under 2\% SoH estimation noise, and maintains this lifetime advantage even under 5\% noise, while sustaining comparable charging speed.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of supercapacitor modelling and SOC, SOH, and RUL estimation techniques for energy management systems
papers.abstract: Supercapacitors function as effective energy storage systems which provide high power output and fast charging and discharging and extended operational time. The precise measurement of state of charge and state of health and remaining useful life presents a major challenge that must be solved for successful energy management system implementation. This review offers an in-depth study which comprehensively examines all supercapacitor modelling methods and advanced estimation techniques that have been developed during recent years. The research assesses different modelling methods which include electrochemical models and equivalent circuit models and fractional-order models and data-driven models according to their accuracy and computational demands and their ability to function in real-world situations. The research investigates the various mechanisms which cause supercapacitors to fail and the aging patterns which result in performance loss. The article presents an extensive examination of techniques used for estimating state of charge and state of health and remaining useful life which includes model-based and data-driven and hybrid methods together with their benefits and drawbacks and their ability to function in real-time. The discussion addresses implementation factors which include sensing accuracy and computational constraints and environmental variability and system integration challenges. The research identifies existing limitations and research gaps and future development paths which will enable the creation of improved supercapacitor management systems that deliver better performance and greater reliability. This review provides essential research material which researchers and engineers can use to improve estimation accuracy and operational safety and lifecycle optimization of advanced supercapacitor energy storage systems.

papers.title: Mineral Particle Suspensions in Carbonate Electrolyte Enable LiF‐Rich Interphases for Durable Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The solid electrolyte interphase in lithium metal batteries determines cycling stability but often suffers from the incomplete decomposition of fluorinated components. Herein, we demonstrate that suspending LiF and Li 2 O particles in a carbonate‐based electrolyte promotes the defluorination of fluoroethylene carbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate. These particles preferentially adsorb fluorinated electrolyte species and induce electronic polarization, thereby modulating their redox reactivity and facilitating interfacial decomposition toward LiF. The generated LiF, together with the trace dissolution and interfacial reprecipitation of suspended LiF particles, continuously enriches the electrode surface with LiF‐rich inorganic species. This process results in the formation of a bilayer interphase on both the lithium metal anode and LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 cathode, featuring a flexible inner layer and a dense LiF‐rich outer layer. The resulting interphase suppresses lithium dendrites, mitigates parasitic reactions, and enables 2400 h of stable cycling in symmetric cells and 85.6% capacity retention after 400 cycles in full cells. By introducing suspended LiF/Li 2 O particles to regulate the interfacial decomposition of fluorinated electrolyte species, this work provides an effective electrolyte‐design strategy for constructing robust interphases in lithium metal batteries.

papers.title: Single-Cycle Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Compressed Continuous Wavelet Features and Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in industrial applications, but their performance gradually degrades over time, making accurate lifetime prediction important for safety and reliability. However, reliable lifetime assessment generally requires extensive degradation testing, which is both costly and time-consuming. To reduce this burden, recent data-driven approaches have sought to predict the end-of-life cycle of batteries from only the initial few cycles. Nevertheless, identifying reliable degradation patterns from such limited early-cycle data remains challenging because early aging dynamics are often subtle and nonlinear. To address this issue, we adopt the continuous wavelet transform to convert cycle-wise voltage, current, and capacity signals into time-frequency representations, enabling multi-resolution characterization of degradation behavior. Building on this representation, we apply scale compression to reduce redundancy while preserving structural information in the scalograms. We evaluate the proposed framework on eight benchmark datasets derived from seven public battery datasets covering diverse electrode chemistries, cell form factors, and cycling protocols. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms prior approaches in single-cycle remaining useful life prediction and remains robust as the number of input cycles increases from 1 to 100. In addition, redundancy-fidelity analysis characterizes the trade-off introduced by scale compression, and gradient-based visual explanations indicate that the model focuses on localized time-frequency regions associated with structured signal transitions during charge-discharge operation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed framework for early-cycle battery remaining useful life prediction.

papers.title: Computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chloride solid-state electrolytes
papers.abstract: Amorphous solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are attractive candidates for safe, high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries. The recent discovery that amorphous LiTaCl$_6$ and LiNbCl$_6$ reach room-temperature ionic conductivities above 10 mS cm$^{-1}$ with activation energies below 0.2 eV has spurred a broad search for new amorphous halide Li conductors. Here we report a computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chlorides (Li-M(III)-Cl) using molecular dynamics driven by a universal machine-learning force field. For the sixteen Li-M(III)-Cl compositions spanning fifteen rare-earth elements and indium, all phases exhibit fast room-temperature Li$^+$ diffusion, with diffusivities of roughly $2$-$5 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$. After scaling the conductivity versus diffusivity relation to an experimental LiTaCl$_6$ reference, the estimated room-temperature conductivities range from 7.7 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$InCl$_6$ to 14 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$. With a low activation energy of 0.18 eV, amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$ is predicted to be among the most conductive amorphous halide electrolytes. To rationalize the composition-dependent transport, we identify two descriptors: the Li$^+$ vibrational density of states (VDOS) center, which correlates inversely with diffusivity, and the average number of correlated bodies in string-like Li$^+$ motion. Compositions in which Li$^+$ has a lower VDOS center and migrates more by individual hopping rather than by concerted motion exhibit higher Li-ion diffusivities. These results suggest rich Li-ion transport characteristics in amorphous halide SSEs.

papers.title: Fractional-Order Model-Based State-of-Charge and State-of-Power Estimation with Available-Capacity Feedback for Lithium-ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-power (SOP) estimation requires consistent treatment of voltage dynamics and available-capacity uncertainty. This study couples a fractional-order equivalent circuit model, a fast multi-innovation unscented Kalman filter SOC observer, and a slow capacity estimator. Self-adaptive learning particle swarm optimization (SLPSO) identifies the model parameters. Capacity feedback links SOC correction to voltage prediction and multi-constraint SOP calculation, with constant-power discharge verification. Compared with a second-order resistor-capacitor model, the fractional-order model reduces voltage root-mean-square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error by 3.45% and 5.82%, respectively. SLPSO reduces the mean final voltage RMSE from 2.215 to 1.561 mV. Across two dynamic profiles and initial SOC values of 0.90 to 1.05, the proposed method yields SOC RMSE values of 0.844% to 0.966%. The fixed-capacity baseline yields 4.9% to 9.8% under initial-SOC mismatch. The maximum capacity-related state-of-health indicator deviation remains below 0.279 percentage points. The maximum discharge-power error is 2.20% for 10 s and below 5% for all 30 s cases. It reaches 8.34% at 30% SOC for 60 s, indicating the need for caution under low-SOC, long-duration operation. These results are limited to fresh-cell tests at 25 °C.

papers.title: Composition-Dependent Electrochemical Performance of Pitch-Derived Carbon-Enhanced Silicon–Graphite Composite Anodes for Lithium-ion Batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract Silicon–graphite composite anodes are high-potential contenders for high-energy lithium-ion batteries, yet their practical application is hindered by the volume expansion of silicon during cycling. In this work, silicon–graphite–pitch composite anodes containing 10–15 wt% micron-sized silicon and 20–25 wt% coal tar pitch is prepared through solution-assisted mixing followed by carbonization. The structural and morphological characterization indicates the coexistence of silicon, graphite and pitch-derived carbon within the composite framework. Electrochemical evaluation demonstrates significantly higher reversible capacities than graphite, delivering initial capacities of ~558 mAh g⁻¹, ~796 mAh g⁻¹ and ~809 mAh g⁻¹ for the samples containing 10%, 12% and 15% silicon, respectively. After 100 cycles at 0.2 mA cm⁻2, the corresponding capacity retentions are 87.44%, 72.03%, and 68.35%. Quantitative irreversible capacity analysis reveals composition-dependent differences in capacity loss, with greater irreversible capacity accumulation in silicon-rich composites. Furthermore, the composite anode containing 12% silicon, when tested in an NMC-811 full-cell configuration, delivers an initial discharge areal capacity of ~2.5 mAh cm⁻² and sustains electrochemical activity over 100 cycles. The study highlights the role of composition on the electrochemical response of silicon–graphite–pitch composites and offers guidance for the design of silicon-based composite anodes for lithium-ion batteries.
